items.text: Senate Republicans looking to avoid a shutdown are weighing a stopgap deal with Democrats that would pay for restocking munitions but withhold money for the Iran war. Appropriations Chair Susan Collins said she is reviewing draft language but does not know how many Republicans would back it. Majority Leader John Thune said he is open to anything that keeps the government funded. Sen. Tim Kaine said Democrats have finalised a proposal barring funds for offensive action against Iran without congressional authorisation, while still allowing spending to protect US troops and evacuate civilians. Democrats want a stopgap at current levels into early next year, when they control both chambers. Republican appropriators would rather pass some full-year bills first, which Sen. Patty Murray called unlikely in the time left. The deadline is Dec 11 and Trump has hinted at vetoes. A University of Maryland/Ipsos poll found 80% of Democrats and 55% of all Americans want the war ended now.
items.outlet: The Washington Post (via Yahoo News); The National
items.notes: WaPo says a shutdown would be the fourth of Trump's second term; The National says the third since he returned to office. Unclear whether Trump would sign such a bill. CNN (Nov 23) carried the same story but was not readable. A right-leaning outlet (BizPac Review) ran the same story under the same framing; it was not read in full.

items.text: Treasury's OFAC sanctioned about 30 targets, 22 entities and 8 individuals, in what it calls Iran's shadow banking system. They include exchange houses, 'rahbar' companies that manage sanctions-evasion networks for Iranian banks, front companies in Dubai, Hong Kong and Türkiye, and the Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold. Secretary Scott Bessent said Iran's economy is in severe trouble and called shadow banking the regime's last financial lifeline. The action uses E.O.s 13902, 13224 and 13871 and adds financial pressure to the naval blockade.
items.notes: Press release dated Nov 23 (US); not in the Nov 24 log.

items.text: Iran is signalling it could send a military-escorted tanker convoy through the US naval blockade. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf said there are military ways to break it, and IRGC-linked outlets claimed dozens of tankers were getting ready to sail for China. Unverified reports say Iran's Supreme National Security Council decided at an emergency session to halt the dispatch of 14 tankers. State broadcaster IRIB denied any convoy had sailed but did not rule one out. Al Jazeera, citing MarineTraffic data, says Hormuz crossings fell more than 40% between Nov 1-7 and Nov 17-23, after more than 25 tankers were hit in a week. There was no new US official statement on a convoy; Trump said on Nov 22 that any blockade runners would end up at the bottom of the sea.
items.notes: The SNSC halt report is unverified and Iranian tanker/mine claims are not independently confirmed. CENTCOM has not commented on the reported Nov 22-23 strike on a tanker near Chabahar (Gulf News).

items.text: Tech stocks gave back part of Monday's rally: the Nasdaq fell 1.48% to 23,734 and the S&P 500 slipped about 0.5% to 7,201, while the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,019, closing above 50,000. Nvidia fell about 5.9% after its 31% jump on Huang's reinstatement, as traders reassessed governance risks and the economics of AI spending. Money rotated into value and defensive stocks, led by healthcare, and Kohl's (+19%) and Dollar Tree (+11%) rose after earnings. The Conference Board's November consumer confidence index was reported at 103.3 against a consensus of about 92, its strongest in nearly two years. The 10-year Treasury yield held around 4.90-4.92%.
items.notes: The 103.3 confidence figure comes from the Motley Fool wrap; a second wrap (citing Reuters) says strongest in nearly two years but gives no number. Not checked against the Conference Board release.

items.text: Sanofi agreed to buy US biotech Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion in equity value and a roughly 46% premium to Insmed's unaffected Nov 18 close. Insmed's main products are Brinsupri (brensocatib), an oral treatment for non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis, and the inhaled antibiotic Arikayce. Sanofi will pay with debt and cash and expects the deal to add to earnings per share by the end of 2028. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to Insmed shareholder and US and other regulatory approvals.

The WSJ, citing people familiar with the plans, and Bloomberg report that USTR Jamieson Greer is about to release Section 301 findings on industrial subsidies and excess capacity in 16 economies, including China, the EU, Japan and South Korea. The findings would be followed by new tariffs that replace the duties the Supreme Court struck down. Partners with deals (EU, Japan, South Korea) are expected to stay at 15% or less, while China would face the steepest rates and India and Vietnam could see higher ones. Steel, aluminium and autos, already covered by Section 232, would likely be excluded. Bloomberg said the announcement could come as soon as Tuesday, but none had been made by Tuesday evening US time.
items.outlet: Seoul Economic Daily; Bombay Samachar (citing WSJ, Bloomberg)
items.notes: Anonymous sourcing; rates, product scope and effective dates not set. WSJ and Bloomberg originals are paywalled and were not read; Axios (Nov 24) also reports it. Relevant to India (US–India thread).

items.text: Lawmakers from both parties promised tougher scrutiny after Huang's reinstatement. Sen. Chris Coons asked what role Huang played in chip sales through Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation) and what harm resulted. Sen. Tom Cotton said Congress will pass bipartisan chip export-control bills, and Sen. Elizabeth Warren urged quick passage. Attorney General Todd Blanche declined to say whether Huang is under investigation, saying the Justice Department would have told Trump if it had evidence of a crime. Trump said he was personally involved in getting Huang reinstated. Huang has a closed House interview on Dec 1 and a public Senate Banking hearing on Dec 3. CNBC notes the Senate hearing falls on the same day as an Nvidia GTC product event.
items.notes: The CNBC article on the GTC clash was seen only as a headline (fetch failed). The TechTimes link was not read in full.

items.text: In a brief unsigned order, the Supreme Court put off Cook County's request to dismiss as moot a challenge to its ban on AR-15-style rifles (Khaya v. Cook County, No. 25-238), saying it will decide the question after oral argument. The county argued the case was moot after named plaintiff Cutberto Viramontes withdrew. It says the remaining challenger, Christopher Khaya, wants an IMI Galil, which it argues falls outside the question; the challengers say he also wants an AR-15-platform rifle. The case is being heard alongside Grant v. Higgins, a challenge to Connecticut's ban. Argument is set for Dec 2, and the ruling could decide whether states may ban such rifles.

On Nov 23, Judge Ana Reyes extended to Dec 12 her temporary restraining order barring the administration from closing East Potomac Park and Hains Point in Washington, except for an imminent safety threat. The order had been due to expire on Nov 28. She cited good cause, because Thanksgiving made it impossible to finish briefing and a hearing before then. A preliminary-injunction hearing is set for Dec 8, with acting NPS Director Jessica Bowron expected to testify. The administration has appealed the TRO to the D.C. Circuit. On Nov 24, Trump attacked Reyes on Truth Social as a Biden-appointed judge blocking the Interior Department's renovation.
items.notes: The FOGOLF piece mixes this extension with her Oct 26 tree-removal injunction, so Newsweek is relied on for the details. No word in either source on the Jessie Liu special master. She rejected DOJ's recusal motion earlier in November.

items.text: A Fourth Circuit panel ruled 2-1 that Virginia can enforce its law, signed by Gov. Abigail Spanberger in April, limiting how local police cooperate with federal immigration agents. The ruling overturned a lower court's temporary block. The panel said the federal government cannot force state and local officials to enforce federal law and that 287(g) agreements can be ended without cause. Virginia cannot stop federal agents from wearing masks, and the law does not bar federal use of private contractors. AG Jay Jones called it a significant victory; the litigation continues.
items.notes: Only WJLA was read; the ARLnow link was not opened.

items.text: A coalition of 21 states, D.C. and Pennsylvania's governor sued HUD in federal court in Massachusetts to block its final rule ending housing aid to any household with a member who lacks lawful immigration status. The rule replaces the current prorated subsidies and takes effect Dec 14. HUD estimates nearly 20,000 mixed-status families are affected, with almost 1,000 needing formal eviction. Plaintiffs put the total at 78,000 people, 55,000 of them eligible. The states say HUD has no authority to rewrite the law and is shifting costs to them. Secretary Scott Turner says the rule ends the exploitation of taxpayer dollars and frees up to $218 million for eligible families on waitlists. Cities and tenant groups have filed separate suits.
items.notes: Filed Nov 23 and missed in the Nov 24 log. The PBS link was not read in full.

items.text: Alaska's Division of Elections certified the midterm results on Nov 23, two days early. Democrat Mary Peltola won the Senate seat outright with 144,583 votes (50.14%), about 12,000 ahead of Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. Certification opens the challenge window: recount requests are due by Nov 26 for governor and lieutenant governor and Nov 28 for other statewide races, and election contests by Dec 3. A federal bid to block certification was dropped, but state and federal investigations involving Peltola's campaign continue. A Hill headline says Sullivan has since conceded.
items.notes: Sullivan's concession is known only from the Hill headline; the article could not be read. Democracy Docket is left-leaning, and ADN's certification story could not be fetched.

items.text: Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) said he will resign on Dec 1 after the House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence that he made unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a staffer in a leadership office. The committee said the conduct could amount to misdemeanour sexual abuse but left any punishment to the full House. Gomez says the encounters were consensual and disputes the report. He had already lost his November re-election bid to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres, so he leaves about a month early.
items.notes: Announced Nov 23 and missed in the Nov 24 log.

items.text: At Justice Department headquarters, Trump signed a memorandum directing AG Todd Blanche to seek the death penalty, where appropriate, for federal murders of minors and murders committed during rape, child sexual abuse, sex trafficking or kidnapping. It also tells the department to speed up executions of existing federal death sentences. He urged Congress to pass Rep. Brandon Gill's Just Punishment for Murder Act. The move targets California Gov. Gavin Newsom's Nov 5 plan to commute all 548 state death sentences. Trump said Newsom sided with murderers; Newsom cited eight exonerations from California's death row and said all those commuted stay in prison for life.
items.notes: The White House text could not be fetched (listed on the presidential-actions page as a Nov 23 memorandum). The ruling-out-deadlines detail comes from Latin Times. CNN and Bloomberg framed it as a 2028 preview against Newsom.

items.text: Trump presented former New York mayor Rudy Giuliani with the Presidential Medal of Freedom at a private White House ceremony on Tuesday, with no press pool invited. Giuliani said he was honoured and humbled. As Trump's lawyer he led efforts to overturn the 2020 election. He owes $148 million in defamation damages to two Georgia election workers, has been disbarred in New York and D.C., and received a federal pardon from Trump in 2025.

Pennsylvania confirmed its ninth measles death of 2026, an unvaccinated Centre County resident, with 1,638 cases and 330 hospitalisations statewide. Wisconsin reported its third death, an adult in Lafayette County, with 920 cases this year, including 88 since Nov 20; 99% were unvaccinated or of unknown status. CDC's weekly count reached 5,838 confirmed cases as of Nov 19, the most since 1991 and more than double 2025's total. CDC lists six deaths nationally without naming states, which Reuters ties to a switch to NCHS mortality data under Secretary Kennedy. HHS said CDC gave Pennsylvania nearly $4 million in emergency response funding. Wisconsin is skipping its Nov 27 update over Thanksgiving, and officials are worried about holiday travel.
items.notes: CDC lists 6 deaths while states report more: PA 9, WI 3, plus VA and NY. CDC data page: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html (as of Nov 19).

items.text: The FDA approved Cogent Biosciences' bezuclastinib (Ekitna) with sunitinib for adults with gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST) previously treated with imatinib. In the Phase 3 PEAK trial, median progression-free survival was 16.5 months with the combination versus 9.2 months with sunitinib alone (hazard ratio 0.50). The label carries a boxed warning for liver toxicity. Cogent says it is the first GIST treatment to beat an active comparator, and trade press calls it the first new GIST drug in about two decades.
items.notes: The FDA press-announcements page could not be fetched (permission not granted). RAPS also lists, without detail, a BridgeBio LGMD2I approval (Nov 23; PDUFA was Nov 27) and Rinvoq for vitiligo. Neither was verified.

items.text: CNN reports, citing a source familiar with the probe, that FAA investigators believe a newly installed router at a remote Arkansas radio site overwhelmed the air traffic control network and caused the Nov 13 nationwide ground stop. An overlooked setting reportedly clashed with the decades-old routers being retired, and investigators reproduced the failure in a lab. The source said investigators are 90% sure bad actors were not involved and that software updates should prevent a repeat. The final report is still being written. The controllers' union says faster maintenance approvals dropped risk reviews, which the FAA denies. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and Secretary Sean Duffy testify on Capitol Hill next week, as Duffy seeks another $50 billion for modernisation.
items.notes: One anonymous source for the cause; no official FAA root-cause release yet.

items.text: Prime Food Processing LLC issued FDA safety warnings for two uneviscerated dried fish products, 7 oz Dried Croaker (lots 24302, 24215) and Dried Herring (lot 25180), because of possible Clostridium botulinum contamination. USDA-FSIS announced a recall of Brett Anthony Foods' WOW BAO Cheeseburger Bao Buns (lot 26243) for undeclared sesame and soy. No illnesses were reported.
items.notes: The FDA notice itself was not opened; details are from eFoodAlert's roundup.

items.text: Russian Ambassador Georgy Mikhno went to the Foreign Ministry in Warsaw on Tuesday after being summoned over the Nov 20 incursion of three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, whose debris fell in Nowy Lipowiec (Lubelskie) and near Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz (Podkarpacie). PAP reported that he attended; according to Goniec and Interia, the ministry said afterwards that he was handed a sharply worded protest note. A day earlier spokesman Maciej Wewiór had said the summons would come only once military and intelligence procedures were complete. Overnight Monday-Tuesday a Russian drone also briefly entered Polish airspace before turning back east. No Russian comment after the meeting was reported.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: Polsat/PAP piece does not detail the note's content; 'very sharp note' wording comes from headlines of Goniec and other outlets citing the MFA (not read in full). Lublin District Prosecutor's Office said on Nov 23 that the three missiles were made in Q4 2026 in Dubna near Moscow and that evidence may support legal-assistance requests and compensation claims (kaszuby24, citing prosecutors' communiqués): https://kaszuby24.pl/trzy-rosyjskie-ch-101-spadly-w-polsce-prokuratura-pociski-z-iv-kwartalu-2026/

items.text: GUS said October retail sales rose 3.5% y/y in constant prices, slightly above the roughly 3.3% consensus, after 5.4% a year earlier; month on month sales were up 7.3%. Seasonally adjusted, sales rose 3.9% y/y and 1.9% m/m. Online sales grew 9.8% y/y in current prices, lifting their share to 9.6%. mBank economists pointed to solid growth in furniture, electronics and household appliances (partly tied to Chinese imports), slower car sales and weak fuel sales that recovered after the CPN fuel-price scheme was relaunched. January-October sales are up 2.7% y/y.

The zloty weakened for a second day: at 16:40 the euro cost 4.4563 zł (intraday high around 4.469) and the franc 4.8614 zł, while the dollar eased to 4.0648 zł after touching about 4.09, its highest since January 2025. BNP Paribas TFI's Izabela Sajdak said the Monetary Policy Council's dovish tone could weigh on the currency; MPC member Ireneusz Dąbrowski said the output gap is not open, supporting steady rates. Bond yields rose in the afternoon after a morning rally.

The Energy Minister's notice published on Nov 24 sets maximum pump prices for Wednesday Nov 25 at 5.84 zł/l for Pb95 (from 5.90), 6.51 zł/l for Pb98 (from 6.56) and 7.23 zł/l for diesel (from 7.32). It is the third phase of the 'Ceny Paliwa Niżej' programme, financed by a 60% tax on excess fuel profits, with fines up to 1m zł for breaches. The caps for Thursday Nov 26 are due in a notice on Nov 25.

Civic Coalition (KO) senators collected signatures on Tuesday to nominate former health minister Izabela Leszczyna to the Monetary Policy Council, with the motion due at the Senate Marshal's office by the Wednesday Nov 25 deadline, according to KO Senate leader Tomasz Grodzki. The Left's Senate club had already nominated economist Prof. Marcin Piątkowski (Koźmiński University), whom Sejm Marshal Włodzimierz Czarzasty called one of Poland's most outstanding economists. The two seats were vacated by Ludwik Kotecki and Przemysław Litwiniuk, who moved to the NBP board. Bankier.pl noted that Leszczyna's move would free her Sejm seat for the next KO candidate on the list, a politician it describes as suspected of corruption.
items.notes: Bankier.pl detail about the replacement MP is from its headline only; article could not be loaded. Formal filing and Senate vote still pending.

items.text: At the V4-plus-Austria meeting at Bratislava Castle on Monday evening, Tusk said he would not accept a 2028-2034 EU budget that raised energy prices, imposed heavy social costs or weakened defence of Poland and the eastern flank, arguing the region needs more EU money, not less. Council President António Costa's negotiating box is about 10% (some €180bn) below the Commission's draft and, per PAP, cuts cohesion policy by 2.4%, while keeping 30% of ETS revenue for the EU budget with a relief mechanism that would benefit Poland. Leaders meet at an extraordinary European Council on Thursday Nov 26. Right-wing outlets (wPolityce, Salon24 blogger Zbigniew Kuźmiuk) argue the budget is bad for Poland and the government is too accommodating, while a presidential adviser told Tysol the summit amounted to an attack on Polish sovereignty.
items.notes: Statement came Monday evening (after yesterday's log was compiled from the pre-meeting TVN24 piece). Right-wing critiques taken from headlines (wPolityce, Tysol) that could not be loaded; framing differs sharply: government outlets stress Tusk's red lines, wPolityce says the government seems satisfied with a 'disastrous' deal.

items.text: President Nawrocki signed the Oct 22 act amending the PIT, CIT and lump-sum tax laws, which reworks tax reliefs from 2027, Infor reported on Nov 24. It abolishes the internet-cost relief (up to 760 zł a year) and the business-expansion relief (up to 1m zł a year), doubles the deduction limit for donations to blood-donor causes and extends the robotisation relief by ten years. Most provisions apply from Jan 1, 2027. This is separate from the larger PIT/CIT rate reform (24% band, higher CIT) passed on Nov 5-6, on which the President has until about Nov 27 to decide.
items.notes: Exact signing date not given in the article; confirm in Dziennik Ustaw. Not to be confused with R-261105-01.

items.text: The Chief Pharmaceutical Inspector (GIF) lifted its May 2026 nationwide suspension of Dolofest, a diclofenac medicated plaster made by Solinea, so it can return to pharmacies. The halt followed a National Medicines Institute finding of a sachet-seal defect in one batch. After the maker submitted new data and the registration authority approved revised seal-integrity parameters, retests in October showed the product met requirements. The decision is dated Nov 20 and was reported on Nov 24.

The Constitutional Tribunal General Assembly's resolutions lifting the immunity of Tribunal President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański, with written reasons, reached the National Prosecutor's Office on Nov 23, RMF FM reported on Tuesday. Prosecutors had said they would not act on media reports, only on the originals; summonses for questioning and charges can now follow, possibly within days. Święczkowski faces three resolutions covering alleged abuse of power as National Prosecutor (2016-2022), irregular supervision of covert operations, and keeping five judges from adjudicating, plus the alleged assault on Judge Maciej Berek; Sochański faces one over blocking judges. The assembly refused consent to detention. TVP Info said a decision on extending Święczkowski's suspension from duties was expected on Wednesday.
items.notes: Contested: government-leaning and centrist outlets (RMF, WP, naTemat) describe a lawful assembly decision; right-wing media (Radio Maryja, wPolsce24) call the Sejm-elected judges 'usurpers' and say the TK president is being denied a defence (headlines only; pages failed to load). No statement from Święczkowski or his lawyer found. No summons confirmed as of Nov 24 evening.

items.text: The Council of Ministers' National Security Committee met at 8:00 on Tuesday, with representatives of the President, PM, Defence Ministry, armed forces and services, to discuss airspace protection, the recent violations, NATO support including AWACS aircraft, and a permanent US base. Kosiniak-Kamysz said the coming weeks would bring decisions of strategic importance for cooperation with the US and NATO; no decisions were announced. Rzeczpospolita added detail on Monday night's incursion: a Russian jet-powered drone crossed near Dorohusk at 22:50, flew about 20 km in, and left after 8-9 minutes before reaching Chełm; no Polish jets were airborne because of weather, and ground systems were cleared to fire but did not. Defence24 says further allied proposals, possibly extra fighters, are to be discussed next week.
items.reporter: Kuba Koprzywa; Marek Kozubal, Robert Biskupski
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: rp.pl may be partly paywalled. Outcome of the committee not reported in sources read.

items.text: The Warsaw District Court extended for three months, to February, the pre-trial detention of Radosław Piesiewicz, former head of the Polish Olympic Committee, in the Zondacrypto investigation. He is charged with paid protection and with favouring some creditors of the threatened crypto exchange; in November prosecutors added a charge of causing over 1m zł in damage to Polska Liga Koszykówki by paying for hotels, restaurants and flights from company funds. His lawyer said the defence will appeal. Separately, a former CBA officer, Artur Ch., was questioned as a suspect; Onet reports he allegedly claimed influence, including with Zbigniew Ziobro, in exchange for benefits, which he denies.
items.notes: Detail of Artur Ch.'s charges comes from Onet via PAP; prosecutors had not published official charges.

items.text: Government spokesman Adam Szłapka said the government will submit another crypto-asset market bill after President Nawrocki vetoed earlier versions and the coalition failed to override. Money.pl reports the new draft is to be even more restrictive, especially on special services' powers to oversee the market, and the government links the crypto sector to Russian financing of sabotage. The President had objected to excessive state interference, strict KNF powers and the risk of firms moving to other EU states. No submission date was given.
items.notes: 'Beyond MiCA' framing is money.pl's interpretation. Poland must implement MiCA supervision; transition deadlines apply.

items.text: ABW officers detained Damian S., 29, who allegedly praised the Nov 7 Kraków attack online and threatened attacks on Nov 11 and 14 that he said would claim ten times more victims. The National Prosecutor's Office charged him with causing a false alarm and publicly praising a crime, saying he meant to intimidate many people while knowing there was no threat. A court ordered one month's detention.

Finance and Economy Minister Andrzej Domański told the Polish Green Transport Forum in Warsaw that Poland will spend almost 100bn zł on transport infrastructure in 2026, about twice the 2023 level, covering roads, rail, ports, high-speed rail, the Port Polska hub and urban transport. He said record public investment must be matched by private investment and that the green transition should build domestic manufacturing rather than rely on imported technology.
items.notes: Speech date not given; article published Nov 24 07:39.

items.text: Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said he had signed a letter asking President Nawrocki to set out in writing what he objects to in the vetoed act implementing the EU Digital Services Act, and proposed a meeting and renewed consultations. The Nov 13 veto blocked a faster procedure for orders restricting access to illegal content such as hate speech; the President cited concerns about expanded blocking powers.
items.notes: Exact date of the letter unclear (Nov 23 or 24); Interia gives no publication date.
